definitions.explanation: A large biting fly that feeds on the blood of mammals. Common in rural and mountainous areas of Japan during summer.

examples.japanese: {虻|あぶ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刺|さ}された→刺す：02111_sasu⟧。
examples.english: I was bitten by a horsefly.
Be careful near the river because there are a lot of horseflies.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{虻|あぶ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飛|と}び{回|まわ}っていて→飛び回る：04610_tobimawaru⟧、⟦{長袖|ながそで}→長袖：15517_nagasode⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}ない→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{何箇所|なんかしょ}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{刺|さ}される→刺す：02111_sasu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In the mountains during summer, horseflies buzz around, and if you don't wear long sleeves you can get bitten in multiple places.

notes:
Often written in hiragana or katakana (アブ) rather than the kanji {虻|あぶ}. Horseflies are a common nuisance in rural Japan, especially near water and livestock. Their bites are painful and can cause significant swelling.

The proverb ⟦{虻蜂取|あぶはちと}らず→虻蜂取らず：06293_abuhachitorazu⟧ (literally "catching neither the horsefly nor the bee") means trying to do two things at once and failing at both — equivalent to the English "between two stools."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虻|あぶ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刺|さ}される→刺す：02111_sasu⟧: to be bitten by a horsefly
- {虻|あぶ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飛|と}ぶ→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧: a horsefly buzzes/flies
- {虻|あぶ}{除|よ}け: horsefly repellent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{蚊|か}→蚊：04294_ka⟧: mosquito — smaller, quieter, bites at night
- ⟦{蜂|はち}→蜂：02242_hachi⟧: bee; wasp — stings rather than bites
- ⟦{蠅|はえ}→蠅：05013_hae⟧: housefly — does not bite, attracted to food and waste
